clue.text: Show up former partner in front of model

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: An ex-partner turns up unexpectedly before a model, embarrassing everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' simply places the first piece before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone up is to reveal their failings publicly, which is what exposing them means.

clue.text: Animal found in earth at end of chase

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the last letter of chase
earth as ground or land

explanation.surface: An animal is run to earth at the end of a hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' places the letter from chase at the front of the earth word.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Finish wine before making forecast

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
end means finish

explanation.surface: Someone finishes the wine before making a prediction.
explanation.walkthrough: The finish comes after the wine in the answer, which is what 'before' arranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to signal or foretell a future event, as an omen does.

clue.text: Arrange to take in Henry and Hilary say for a limited period

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to sort is to arrange
H is the symbol for the henry, a unit of inductance
Hilary is a term at Oxford and in the English law courts

explanation.surface: A plan to host Henry and Hilary only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry and Hilary' look like two guests; Hilary is the spring term at Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-term arrangement is one meant to last only a brief time.

clue.text: Behind when explosion interrupts races – just the opposite

indicators.note: breaking into something puts one part in the middle of the other
reversing the stated roles means the interrupter becomes the thing interrupted, swapping inside and outside

blocks.note: a boom is the sound of an explosion
the TT races are the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A spectator wonders what lies behind a blast that disrupts a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the explosion goes inside the races; 'just the opposite' tells you to put the races inside the explosion instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind as a noun is a colloquial word for the buttocks, which the bottom also names.

clue.text: Against song being broadcast

blocks.note: leaning against a wall is leaning on it
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A protest song gets radio airplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on air is being transmitted live on radio or television.

clue.text: Reproduced letters of support

indicators.note: something reproduced is made again, here in a new arrangement

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Copies of letters backing a campaign are circulated.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework that holds up a table top, a structural support.

clue.text: Knock around with workers near the centre of Hartlepool

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters only

blocks.note: two words for a worker, man and hand
the two middle letters of the ten-letter town name

explanation.surface: Labourers get roughed up in the middle of Hartlepool, a port town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle someone is to treat them roughly, pushing them about.

clue.text: Continue to play around

blocks.note: first meaning: keep going
second meaning: misbehave, or have an affair

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to keep fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are phrasal verbs; the second is the British idiom also behind the Carry On comedy films.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to proceed without stopping and to behave in a rowdy or flirtatious way.

clue.text: Call soldiers from the rear to contain Nationalist parade

to contain is to hold something within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to page someone is to call them over a speaker
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
N is a standard abbreviation for Nationalist

explanation.surface: Troops are summoned to marshal a nationalist march.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a public procession or show, much like a parade.

clue.text: Practise with Sue

second meaning: take legal action against

explanation.surface: Rehearsing together with someone called Sue.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue looks like a woman's name, but it is the legal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute is both to pursue an activity, as in prosecuting a war, and to bring legal proceedings.

clue.text: Drake perhaps coming to the queen after game is over

indicators.note: something turned over is upside down, so the letters run the other way
after sends the royal abbreviation to the end, behind the game

explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Drake finishing his game of bowls before facing the Armada, then reporting to his queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Drake was an Elizabethan explorer and privateer, an example of a daring adventurer.

clue.text: Starts to tip messily over each side

the opening letter of messily

explanation.walkthrough: The two opening letters go either side of the abbreviation, one in front and one behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team in sport, as in picking sides for a match.

clue.text: Theologian introduced to drink becomes muddled

clue.text: Concern for a forward in agony

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: American writes about the onset of despair after son hangs

the onset of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
US for American
to pen is to write
the first letter of despair

explanation.walkthrough: 'after son' puts the son's letter at the front, ahead of the American.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it from above.

clue.text: Easily offended members of sect supporting girl without question

clue.text: Prevalent in a long adventure movie featuring Ms Moore

clue.text: Laura playing around caught by daughter in this novel

letters to rearrange

clue.text: Wise to follow university’s customary practice

blocks.note: U for university

clue.text: One playing right back blocking passes easily at start of season

the first letter of season

clue.text: Somewhat rare artefacts discovered in field
